title: Ted Lasso Season 4 Trailer Drops: A Women's Team, New Faces, and a Fresh Start
summary:
Imagine a coach so optimistic he makes biscuits for his boss and believes in believe signs. That's Ted Lasso, and he's back for a fourth season on Apple TV starting August 5. The new trailer, released July 28, reveals a surprising pivot: Ted will coach a second-division women's soccer team in Richmond, England. It's a bold move after season 3's seemingly definitive ending, where Ted handed the reins to Roy Kent and returned to Kansas to be with his son.

The trailer packs in classic Lasso charm — folksy wisdom, awkward hugs, and the return of the will-they-won't-they tension between certain characters. Jason Sudeikis reprises his role, joined by Hannah Waddingham as Rebecca Welton, Brett Goldstein as Roy Kent, and other fan favorites. The 10-episode season runs through October 7.

Ted Lasso was a cultural juggernaut, earning 61 Emmy nominations and winning Best Comedy for its first two seasons. But season 3 divided fans with questionable character arcs and a wrapped-up story. Co-creator Sudeikis had originally planned a three-season arc, making the 2025 renewal a surprise. Yet this reset — coaching a new team — could recapture the show's wholesome magic without undoing its past. The trailer suggests a return to the heartfelt humor that made us fall for the mustachioed coach. Whether it lives up to the early brilliance remains to be seen, but one thing's for sure: we'll be watching.
why_it_matters: This story shows how stories themselves can evolve — even after a seemingly perfect ending, creators can find new directions that reflect a changing world, like the growth of women's sports. For viewers, it's a lesson in second chances and how optimism can be applied in fresh, unexpected ways.

background_read: Ted Lasso began as a comedic character played by Jason Sudeikis in 2013 NBC Sports commercials, designed to promote the English Premier League in America. The concept was later developed into a full series for Apple TV+ (Apple's streaming platform, launched in 2019), premiering in August 2020 when audiences craved uplifting stories during the COVID-19 pandemic.

It quickly became a global hit, racking up 61 Emmy nominations (the television equivalent of the Oscars) and winning Best Comedy for its first two seasons. Sudeikis and co-creator Bill Lawrence originally mapped out a three-season arc, which concluded in season 3 with Ted returning to Kansas and handing his team to assistant coach Roy Kent.

That ending seemed definitive, making the surprise 2025 renewal for a fourth season all the more unexpected. The new season shifts focus to a women's team in Richmond (a fictional London neighborhood named after the real Richmond upon Thames), a bold move that could allow the series to explore new themes while keeping its signature heart.

perspectives.description: Fans and the cast celebrate the return of a beloved character who promotes kindness and mental well-being at a time when the world still craves comfort. The shift to a women's team could bring a new audience and highlight underrepresented athletes.

Some worry the show risks tarnishing its legacy by extending beyond the intended ending, much like other series that overstayed their welcome. The pivot might feel forced, and the absence of some original cast chemistry could disappoint loyal viewers.

The renewal reflects a broader TV industry pattern where streaming platforms revive successful IP to retain subscribers. Ted Lasso's season 4 is a commercial calculation as much as a creative one, reflecting how art and commerce often collide in the streaming era.

If the new season succeeds, it could inspire more mainstream shows to center around women's sports, which historically receive less screen time. It might also encourage storytellers to take bold narrative risks, knowing that audiences are open to resetting beloved worlds rather than simply continuing them.
